newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary O/N rates end up on tight yearend market.
newsitem.headline: Hungary O/N rates end up on tight yearend market.

text.p: Hungary's overnight interest rates closed higher at 25.25 percent as the market became short on factors typical for the year-end, dealers said.
The overnight rates moved between 24.75 and 25.5 percent, compared with Thursday's 25 percent end, what dealers already called high.
"The market has run out of money," said Csaba Nagy of Europai Kereskedelmi Bank. "It could be felt on Tuesday and Wednesday already, as banks sold foreign currencies to create forints on the market."

Dealers added that increasing demand for the forint pressed it to a distance of some 25 fillers from the central bank bid on the foreign currency market down from 40 to 50 pips usual in the past two weeks.

The demand may have been created by closing futures positions on Hungary's bourses ahead of ther yearend, by the tax-payment deadline on Sunday and payments for government bonds sold at recent auctions, dealers said.
They added that Friday was the last working day of the commercial banks' reserve period, and the banks may also have needed money to replenish their reserves.
But the overnight rates were likely to drop on Monday, dealers said. Nagy added they would probably find support at around 22.5 percent early next week.
